newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Quiet but prices supported.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Quiet but prices supported.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market was quiet on Wednesday with no deals heard done in late Asian day but prices were well supported, traders said.
Offers for the 180-cst grade were seen at $99.50 per tonne and the 380-cst grade was at $99.50 but bids were scarce.
They said a local trading company, which has been buying steadily since late June, was absent from the market but some said demand from the trading company is still there.
"I think he still needs to buy to cover his term contracts," said one trader. "Only that the buying is small and he apparantly does not want to push up prices."
Traders have said the $100-per-tonne level is an immediate resistance for the 180-cst grade.
On Tuesday, a 380-cst cargo was traded at $95 per tonne and a 180-cst grade exchanged hands at $98 per tonne.
Fuel oil swaps edged up slightly, with August last quoted at $98.75/$99.50.
On Wednesday, Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) bought two 0.5-percent sulphur fuel oil cargoes for September delivery at $120 and $129 per tonne.

The first 38,000-tonne low-pour cargo, bought at around $129 per tonne, will be for September 1-10 delivery and the second high-pour cargo, bought at $120 per tonne, will be for September 21-30, a company source said.

"We didn't buy enough for September this time because we are not happy with the prices," said the source, adding that CPC would issue another fuel oil tender in the next few weeks for September cargoes.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
